subject: Post-call: data retention carveout / 0-retention clarification for NeuroScripts
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Patel <t.patel@neuroscripts.com>, Lucy Huang <lucy@neuroscripts.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call: data retention carveout / 0-retention clarification for NeuroScripts

Hi Tom and Lucy —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of the ask and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

- Ask (legal/prod): NeuroScripts needs a firm path to either (A) 0-retention for user prompt & response pairs that contain PII, or (B) a tightly scoped short retention window (7 days) for KV/cache logs and non-PII telemetry for debugging.
- Risk/controls requested: KMS-managed keys (customer-provided preferred), limited audit log exposure, SOC 2 evidence, and contract language for the retention carveout in the DPA.
- Timeline: procurement expects vendor security sign-off by 2027-01-12 to hit their Q1 pilot start.

What we can do today (high-level):
1) Redwood can support an ephemeral mode where request/response payloads are not persisted to long-term logs and KV cache TTLs can be set to 0–7 days depending on workload characteristics.
2) For absolute 0-retention on PII, we'd propose a hybrid approach: enable prefix/KV cache eviction and disable long-term telemetry ingestion for those routes, plus explicit contract language/attestation. Note: there are limitations around model-heavy diagnostics (e.g., we cannot give per-token reconstruction of in-flight soft-state without some ephemeral caching).
3) KMS integrations: we support customer-managed KMS (AWS/GCP) for encryption-at-rest and can provide HSM-backed key attestations.

Immediate next steps I propose:
- I will circulate a redlined DPA that includes the retention carveout language for your legal team to review (attached).
- Ben (cc'd) will run a short feasibility doc mapping 0-retention to our routing/caching layers and call out any edge cases.
- If you can share the minimal list of endpoints that require 0-retention, we’ll draft an operational runbook for the pilot.

Attached: neuroscripts-dpa-redline.pdf (high-level redlines + two alternative clause wordings). Also linking our short note on ephemeral modes.

Proposed call: Wed 2026-12-22 10:00 AM ET to align on the endpoints and procurement asks — is that still good for you?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0194
[Attachment: neuroscripts-dpa-redline.pdf (PDF)]
From: Tom Patel <t.patel@neuroscripts.com>

Cc: Ana Santos <ana.santos@neuroscripts.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 09:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call: data retention carveout / 0-retention clarification for NeuroScripts

Jordan — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Legal will push hard for an absolute 0-retention guarantee for any content that includes PII. If that can't be contractually guaranteed, they'll accept a bounded 7-day maximum with an audit of deletion operations.
- Prod cares about debugability: they want a safe way to repro issues (trace ids, non-PII metrics). They suggested keeping short-lived request IDs and aggregated metrics only.
- Procurement: our SOW/PO needs to be in place by 2027-01-10 to start the trial by end of month.

I've attached Ana from procurement — she’ll coordinate the vendor paperwork and timeline. Also, can your team confirm whether Redwood backs up any production logs to long-term storage (cold backups) by default? That’s a red flag for us unless we can opt out.

Tom
CTO, NeuroScripts Inc.
[t.patel@neuroscripts.com | +1 617-555-2201]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Patel <t.patel@neuroscripts.com>, Lucy Huang <lucy@neuroscripts.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Dec 2026 12:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Post-call: data retention carveout / 0-retention clarification for NeuroScripts

Tom — appreciate the clarity. Quick answers inline: 

- Backups: by default Redwood does replicate critical runtime metadata for disaster recovery, but customers can opt-out of long-term backups for specific routes and datasets. For your pilot we can configure the account so that any route tagged as "neuroscripts-pii" will not be archived to cold backup. We will document the operational steps and provide attestation.
- 0-retention feasibility: Our Security team says we can support contractual 0-retention for payloads if NeuroScripts agrees to the operational constraints we discussed (no server-side debugging snapshots, no model eval capture for those routes). Ben will outline the edge cases where ephemeral state is still required for latency/caching and show mitigations.

Ben — could you confirm the following in the feasibility note before Wed’s call?
1) What happens to performance when KV cache TTL=0 for high-throughput routes? (expected latency hit)
2) How we can scope logs to aggregated metrics + trace IDs without recording raw prompts/responses.
3) Backup opt-out steps and audit trail generation for deletion/eviction events.

Tom/Lucy — I'll also ask Legal to put the two alternative clause wordings into DocuSign so you can track edits. DocuSign link will go out after internal approval.

Jordan

Tom/Jordan — following up with the technical sketch I promised. High level:

1) KV/cache TTL=0 behavior
- If we set KV TTL=0 for an endpoint, any in-memory state will be evicted immediately after request completion. This removes long-term retention risk but will increase cold-starts for repeated conversational context; expected median latency increase ~80–150ms depending on model and sequence length. We can mitigate via client-side context stitching (we provide SDK helpers) and adaptive prefix caching for non-PII tokens.

2) Logs and metrics
- We can emit only aggregated counters and trace IDs for observability. Trace IDs are opaque strings and won’t contain raw prompt content. Audit trail for deletion/eviction events is writable to your account-specific audit log (accessible only to NeuroScripts admins) and can be configured to keep a deletion record without the payload.

3) Backups/archives
- Normal backups exclude route-level exclusions when opt-out is configured. We will document the opt-out and provide a signed attestation (PDF) once enabled.

Attached: redwood-ephemeral-data-options.pdf — this is a short note covering performance tradeoffs and sample configs.

Next steps I recommend before the Wed alignment call:
- NeuroScripts to list the endpoints that must be 0-retention (JSON array or bullet list)
- Procurement to confirm PO/SOW timeline.
- Legal: propose which clause (A = absolute 0-retention, B = 7-day max) to start with for negotiation.

Happy to jump on Wed and run through a tech demo of the opt-out configuration.

Best,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
